work.title: St Matthew Passion
work.movement: No. 1. Kommt, ihr Töchter, helft mir klagen — opening chorus; a selected highlight from a complete recording, not the complete Passion

version.note: The performing edition is not identified. The booklet gives the composition as Leipzig 1729 or earlier, revised 1736, and cites the autograph score Mus. ms. Bach P 25 and the parts St 110. The booklet and the Bach-Gesellschaft score number this chorus No. 1; the New Bach Edition also numbers it 1.

value.name: Münchener Chorknaben
value.role: boys’ choir, ripieno soprano (chorale ‘O Lamm Gottes, unschuldig’)

performers.note: The booklet track list gives the chorale to the Knabenchor. The booklet also names instrumental soloists for the whole Passion (flutes Walther Theurer and Wolfgang Haag; oboes Edgar Shann and Kurt Hausmann; organ Ekkehard Tietze and Hedwig Bilgram; double bass Franz Ortner; bassoon Karl Kolbinger; viola da gamba Oswald Uhl), and Fritz Rothschuh as chorus master. Their assignment to this number is not stated, so they are not listed as performers of it.

date.value: 23 June – 21 August 1958 (sessions 23 June–6 July, 11–12 August and 21 August)
date.note: The Archiv Produktion LP labels print the recording dates as 6/23–7/6, 8/11–12 and 21/1958; the retail page gives 23 June–6 July, 11–12 and 21 August 1958; the booklet essay gives 22 sessions between 23 June and 21 August 1958 and its credit line gives 6–8/1958. Which session produced No. 1 is not stated.

label.value: Archiv Produktion (Deutsche Grammophon Gesellschaft, History of Music Division)
label.note: The labels read ‘Archive Production — History of Music Division Deutsche Grammophon Ges.’ and ‘Stereo’.

catalogue.value: SAPM 198 009/012 (first stereo edition, four LPs); the scanned export pressing carries ARC 73 125–73 128 / SAPM 198 625–628
catalogue.note: First release year is disputed in the sources: the booklet and Wikipedia say 1959 (the booklet reads ‘LPs released/veröffentlicht/paru 1959’ and prints ℗ 1959 Deutsche Grammophon); Discogs and the Internet Archive LP catalogue give 1958, which is the recording year. Both dates precede 1963. The digital file used here is a later remaster, not the LP.

matrixTakeSides.value: First stereo edition: first programme side of the set (Discogs side A), first track (9:50 on the LP); matrix and take numbers not read
matrixTakeSides.note: The side and position come from the Discogs tracklist only, whose first edition is automatically coupled, so the programme side is not the physical side of a particular LP. No run-out inscription was seen, so matrix and take are unknown.

credits.note: No remastering engineer or studio is credited in the item metadata or the booklet. The booklet’s © 2001 Deutsche Grammophon notice and the retail page’s ‘Digitally remastered’ line show only that commercial digital releases exist. The upload is a private Internet Archive upload in the hifidelity collection.

date.note: No transfer date is established. The Internet Archive item was created on 16 February 2026; that upload date is not a transfer date.

processing.value: 24-bit/192 kHz FLAC (item description ‘1959 [FLAC 24-192]’), digitally remastered according to the retail page; streamed here through the Internet Archive’s VBR MP3 derivative.
processing.note: The item’s track titles and durations (9:49 for this track) match the retail page’s 2016 hi-res listing, so the file is probably that release, but the item names no source. No speed correction, noise reduction or restoration settings are stated.

digital.format: Internet Archive VBR MP3 derivative (14,109,635 bytes) of the uploaded 24-bit FLAC (589.35 s); the FLAC itself is over 100 MB and was not downloaded

composition.value: Bach’s composition (d. 1750) and the Bach-Gesellschaft edition used for the orchestra view (Breitkopf & Härtel, 1854) are public domain.
composition.note: IMSLP catalogues the Bach-Gesellschaft volume as Public Domain. This does not clear the sound recording, the later remaster or the booklet’s prose.

recording.value: territorial — European recording-rights expiry; first publication documented before 1963 (Archiv Produktion stereo LP edition, 1958 or 1959).
recording.note: Programme rule 3. The recording was made in June–August 1958 and first issued on four stereo LPs; the booklet states 1959 and quotes a critic’s review of the four LPs from May 1959. Whether the first issue fell in 1958 or 1959, a recording published by 1959 had exhausted the ordinary EU 50-year phonogram term (to the end of 2009) before the extension that applied from 1 November 2013. This is territorial, not a licence: the Internet Archive item carries no licence URL and no Public Domain Mark. US status is not established and no US public-domain claim is made. The audio file is a later commercial digital remaster; this dossier relies on the first publication of the recording and does not separately clear any rights claimed in the remastering, which is a point for the integration lead.

rights.creditLine: J. S. Bach, St Matthew Passion, BWV 244: No. 1, Kommt, ihr Töchter, helft mir klagen. Münchener Bach-Chor, Münchener Chorknaben, Münchener Bach-Orchester; Karl Richter. Recorded June–August 1958, Herkulessaal, Munich. Archiv Produktion SAPM 198 009/012, first issued 1958–59. Digital remaster via the Internet Archive. European recording-rights expiry only; US status unestablished.
